newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT-VocalTec cut to hold.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-VocalTec cut to hold.

text.p: Josephthal Lyon & Ross said it had downgraded VocalTec Ltd to a hold after the over-the-counter share soared 112 percent in the past two weeks.
Josephthal also cut its earnings estimate for the Israeli company to a 1997 loss of $1.02 a share from a loss of $0.95 and to a loss of $0.42 in 1998 from a loss of $0.38.

Josephthal said it does not expect full deployment of VocalTec's gateway products before 1998. It also said operating expenses were likely to increase next year due to an expansion in operations. In 1996 VocalTec lost $0.71 a share.
VocalTec closed at $13-5/8 on Wednesday, surpassing Josephthal's 12-month price target of $10.
Behind the price surge was an announcement from Deutsche Telekom concerning the launching of an Internet telphony pilot and news of VocalTec's alliances with AT&T and Motorola.
In addition, a Frost & Sullivan report named VocalTec as the leader in its field, based on 1996 sales figures.

"Investor response to these announcements clearly reinforces our assessment that VocalTec is and will continue to be a volatile news-driven stock. While we expect more positive news from VocalTec that will bring both Internet telephony and VocalTec to the forefront, the timing of this news is unclear," analyst Abraham Finklestein said in a report.
"In our opinion, the stock should trend back to the $10 level, at which point we would become more aggressive buyers."
